title: RetryWoo: failed-payment recovery for WooCommerce subscription stores
source: Top 50 research (Nov 2026): reframed from ideas dropped from the Top 25 report, plus new web research
summary: Subscription stores lose customers when cards expire or payments fail. RetryWoo is a WooCommerce plugin plus cloud service that retries payments at smart times, warns customers before cards expire, and sends one-click card-update links by email and SMS.
hook: "Every month about 60 coffee subscriptions just stop because a card failed. Most of those people never meant to cancel."
story:
**Lena runs a coffee subscription shop on WooCommerce** with about **1,400 active subscribers** paying €19 a month. Every month around **5% of renewals fail**: expired cards, bank declines, insufficient funds. WooCommerce sends one generic email and retries a few times on a fixed schedule.

She sees the subscription count drop but doesn't know that **most of those customers never chose to leave**. Tools like Churnkey or Baremetrics Recover are built for software companies on Stripe Billing and cost more than she wants to pay. She wants a plugin that installs in ten minutes and shows: "this month we saved 41 subscriptions, worth €779 a month".
whyNow: Involuntary churn from failed payments is a well-documented, measurable loss, and the known recovery tools focus on Stripe-billed SaaS. WooCommerce subscription stores (coffee, pet food, beauty, courses, memberships) are a big, under-served group that buys through the WordPress plugin directory.
evidence: About 22% of SaaS churn is involuntary (study of 5.4M failed payments); Recurly puts it at 20–26% of B2B SaaS churn [Churnkey]
Failed payments cost about 9% of recurring revenue a year (attributed to Stripe, secondary source) [Lago]
Baremetrics Recover's add-on price rose from $158 to $208 a month in 2025 [PricingSaaS]
Churn Buster keeps pricing behind a sales call; a third-party tracker lists $149/month, unverified [Churn Buster / Toolradar]
Many indie dunning tools exist for Stripe SaaS (e.g. WorkAid Dunning), which shows demand but also crowding [Indie Hackers]

whyReal.title: Money lost every month
whyReal.text: Each failed renewal is a customer who usually wanted to stay. The loss shows up directly in the store's revenue.

whyReal.title: Easy to prove value
whyReal.text: The product can show exactly how many subscriptions and how much revenue it saved, which makes the price easy to justify.

whyReal.title: Dunning is crowded, WooCommerce less so
whyReal.text: Most recovery tools are built around Stripe Billing for SaaS. WooCommerce subscription stores use different plugins and payment gateways.

whyReal.title: A real channel
whyReal.text: The WordPress plugin directory and WooCommerce marketplace bring buyers without cold calls.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: WooCommerce stores with 200–10,000 active subscriptions: coffee, food boxes, pet supplies, beauty, memberships and courses.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The store owner or e-commerce manager.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: Global in English through the WordPress plugin directory, WooCommerce agencies and subscription-commerce communities.

solution.title: Install the plugin
solution.text: connects to WooCommerce Subscriptions and the store's payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, Mollie) and reads failed renewals.

solution.title: Smart retries
solution.text: retries at better times (after payday, different time of day, by decline reason) instead of a fixed schedule.

solution.title: Pre-expiry warnings
solution.text: emails and SMS customers whose card expires next month, with a one-click update link (no login needed).

solution.title: Friendly recovery messages
solution.text: AI writes short messages in the store's tone and language, sent by email and SMS over 2–3 weeks.

solution.title: Recovery dashboard
solution.text: shows failed, recovered and lost subscriptions and the monthly revenue saved.

later: Pause or downgrade offers instead of cancelling

techStack: Cloud service in Node.js or Python

timeline.what: Find 30 WooCommerce subscription stores; ask for their monthly failed-payment numbers; offer a free "lost revenue report".
Plugin, failed-renewal sync, retry rules, card-update page.
Email sequences, pre-expiry warnings, dashboard, billing; 5 beta stores.
WordPress.org free version listing, SMS add-on, case study with real recovered revenue.

competitors.name: WooCommerce Subscriptions built-in retries
competitors.what: Basic fixed retry schedule and emails
competitors.gap: No smart timing, no pre-expiry warnings, little reporting

competitors.name: Churnkey, Baremetrics Recover, Churn Buster
competitors.gap: Built mainly for Stripe-billed SaaS; higher or sales-led pricing

competitors.name: Indie Stripe dunning tools
competitors.gap: Stripe Billing only, not WooCommerce subscriptions

competitors.name: Us
competitors.what: WooCommerce-native recovery with smart retries and card-update links
competitors.gap: Installs in minutes, priced for small stores, shows saved revenue

risks.risk: WooCommerce or payment gateways improve built-in retries
risks.answer: Focus on pre-expiry warnings, messaging and reporting, which gateways do not do well.
Price by active subscriptions so larger stores pay more; aim for stores with 500+ subscribers.
This is a plugin-directory and content play; Jonatan can help by contacting WooCommerce agencies as resellers.
Never store card data; use the gateway's hosted card-update pages.

questions: How many subscription renewals fail each month, and what happens next?
Which subscription plugin and payment gateway do you use?
Do you know how many failed customers come back on their own?
Have you tried any recovery tool? Why did you stop or not start?
If a plugin showed it saved you €500+ a month, what would you pay for it?

numbers.competition: Crowded for Stripe SaaS, thin for WooCommerce
numbers.whoSells: Victor → plugin directory and content; Jonatan → Woo agencies
